title: Grace Periods, Default Counts and Rebill Due Dates of the Payment Arrangements
content:
**Credit and Collections Policy — Schedule D: missed installments and default, Payment Arrangements (Deferred Payment Agreements)**

| Tier | Grace period after a bill's due date | Missed installments that put the agreement in default | Current charges of the bill must be paid with the installment | Billed-back balance due after the default date | Disconnection on the original notice without a new notice period |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Standard Deferred Payment Agreement | 5 calendar days | 1 | yes | 0 days (due on issue) | yes |
| Extended Hardship Payment Agreement | 10 calendar days | 2 | yes | 10 calendar days | no |
| Winter Protection Payment Agreement | 10 calendar days | 2 | yes | 10 calendar days | no |
| Medical Certificate Payment Agreement | 10 calendar days | 2 | yes | 10 calendar days | no |
| Agricultural Harvest Payment Agreement | 5 calendar days | 1 | yes | 0 days (due on issue) | yes |
| Commercial Installment Agreement | 0 calendar days | 1 | yes | 0 days (due on issue) | yes |

**Schedule D definitions**

- *Grace period*: the calendar days after a bill's due date within which an installment may still be paid before it counts as missed. The Commercial Installment Agreement allows none.
- *Default count*: the number of missed installments, a whole number, that puts the agreement in default.
- *Current charges paid with the installment*: whether the current charges of each bill must also be paid with the installment for the installment to count as paid. Every tier says yes.
- *Billed-back balance due*: the calendar days after the default date by which the billed-back balance is due; 0 means due on issue.
- *Disconnection on the original notice*: whether a defaulted account may be disconnected on the original notice without a new notice period.

**Comparisons drawn from Schedule D**

- One missed installment puts a Standard Deferred Payment Agreement, an Agricultural Harvest Payment Agreement or a Commercial Installment Agreement in default; the Extended Hardship, Winter Protection and Medical Certificate tiers default at the second.
- The three tiers that default at one miss are also the three whose billed-back balance is due on issue and whose defaulted account may be disconnected on the original notice.
